title: Historical carbon dioxide emissions caused by land-use changes are possibly larger than assumed
problem: Dynamic global vegetation models likely underestimate historical CO₂ emissions from land-use change by neglecting key processes like tree harvesting and shifting cultivation, thus creating large uncertainties in the magnitude of the terrestrial carbon sink and its future potential to sequester carbon.
method: The paper uses a multi-model analysis with dynamic global vegetation models to re-evaluate historical carbon emissions by incorporating previously ignored land management processes, such as shifting cultivation, wood harvesting, and grazing, into the simulations.
task: The task is to re-quantify historical carbon dioxide emissions from land-use change by incorporating overlooked processes, such as shifting cultivation and wood harvesting, into dynamic global vegetation model simulations to show that these emissions have been underestimated.

innovation: Using dynamic global vegetation models, this paper argues that historical CO₂ emissions from land-use change are substantially underestimated because key processes like wood harvesting and shifting cultivation have been ignored, which implies a correspondingly larger terrestrial carbon sink.

JULES model. Here, to implement crop harvest, four additional PFTs were added: C3 crops, C4 crops, C3 pasture and C4 pasture, with identical parameter sets as the C3 and C4 grass PFTs. Lotka-Volterra equations52 are used three times to calculate the vegetation distribution in natural areas, crop and pasture areas, with the calculations in each area being independent of the others.

JSBACH model. The JSBACH version used here is similar to the version in ref. 1. S3 experiments include gross land-use transitions and WH21. FLULCCC.O in Supplementary Table 2 were calculated by subtracting the individual contributions of these processes. Net transitions are derived from the gross transition implementation, but by minimizing land conversions²¹. WH' is taken not only from forest PFTs but also shrubs and natural grasslands are harvested.

LPJ-GUESS model. SC: For implementing SC, recommendations followed those by ref. 7, with rotation periods of 15 years. Simulations used the coupled carbon-nitrogen version of the model 42,53 spin-up used constant 1701 land-cover and CO₂ concentration, and 1901-1930 recycled climate. Upon steady-state land-cover and CO₂ were allowed to change from 1701, and climate from 1901 onwards42. When land is cleared, 76% of woody biomass and 71% of leaf biomass is removed and oxidised within one year, with a further 21% of woody biomass assigned to a product pool with 25 year turnover time42. Upon abandonment a secondary forest stand is created and recolonization of natural vegetation takes place from a state of bare soil.

LPJ model. Compared to previous versions, the model now uses the World Harmonization Soils Database v.1.2 for soil texture and Cosby equations55 to estimate soil water holding capacity. Further developments allow for gross land-use transitions and WH to be prescribed.

LPJmL model. The LPJmL version used was as described in refs 56–58. In the baseline scenario all crops were simulated as a mixture of C3 and C4 managed grasslands, 50% of the aboveground biomass is transferred to the harvest compartment and assumed to be respired in the same year.

LP3X model. Land-use change, including SC and WH, is implemented as described in ref. 20, using the full land-use transition and WH data provided". Wood (heartwood and sapwood) removed by harvesting and land conversion is diverted to products pools with turnover rates of 2 years (37.5%) and 20 years (37.5%). The rest, including slash from roots and leaves is respired within the same year.

OCN model. The OCN version used here is applied as in the framework of the annual carbon budget¹. OCN includes interactive C and N cycling with N deposition and N fertilizer inputs60. WH was implemented by first satisfying the prescribed wood extraction rate from wood production due to land-use change, and then removing additional biomass proportionally from forested tiles.

ORCHIDEE model. WH: Developments to the version included in ref. 1 include annual WH, the total wood harvested of a grid cell is removed from above-ground biomass of the different forest PFTs proportional (i) to its fraction in the gridcell and (ii) also to its relative biomass among forest PFTs. This results in harvesting more wood in biomass-rich forests.

VISIT model. Implementation of climate, land-use change (gross transitions, SC) and WH has not changed from¹. Land-use, land-use change and WH data for 1860–2014 were from LUH17. For WH, the amount of harvested biomass prescribed in ref. 7 were transferred from simulated stem biomass to 1-year product pool (emitted in entirety in same year of wood harvest), 10-year product pool, and 100-year product pool in a same manner as in the cleared biomass with land-use change described in ref. 67.
